Subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval - follow-up & next tests

Hi Tom / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps for the competitive evaluation vs the hyperscaler offering you mentioned: 

1) Goal of the evaluation
- Validate cost/latency tradeoffs for your production workload (document ingestion -> 1-shot retrieval+generate flows).
- Confirm capacity guarantees (reserved capacity) for peak batch inference and sustained throughput.

2) Key differentiators we discussed (what Redwood brings)
- Dedicated capacity with SLA-backed latency & uptime (reserved GPU pools + autoscale policies).
- Smart routing + quantization profiles to reduce per-token cost while preserving quality.
- Built-in prefix/KV caching to cut repeated-token costs for chat-like workflows.

3) Proposed tests (we can run these in parallel against your hyperscaler tests):
- Latency P50/P95 at 256/512 token responses (single request and 8/16 concurrent clients).
- Throughput soak: 24h sustained run at target QPS to confirm warm caches & reserved pool behavior.
- Burst behavior: large spiky load for 30m to verify burst capacity and pre-warm times.
- Failure/fallback: simulate node loss and validate automatic fallback to compatible model variant.
- Cost modeling: run identical request mix to compare effective $/1M tokens (inc. egress & reserved costs).

4) Data/setup we need from your side
- A representative prompt set (10-20 queries) + typical token budgets.
- Preferred sequence lengths and concurrency expectations.
- Any security/compliance constraints (VPC, KMS) if we need to run on a Private deployment.

Attachments: I attached a short redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.xlsx and a draft acme_poc_scope.pdf that maps the tests above to timelines.

Proposed next steps / dates:
- POC kickoff (90m): Wed 22 Jul or Thu 23 Jul — confirm preferred slot.
- Run baseline throughput + latency tests (day 1), run soak + burst tests (day 2).

If that plan looks good I can lock in the slots and loop in infra to reserve a dedicated pool for your POC.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—Markus Klein
Senior Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

Tom / Markus —

Quick technical clarifications on reserved capacity and the proposed tests: 

- Reserved capacity on Redwood = dedicated GPU pool (customer-isolated). You get guaranteed baseline vGPU hours and minimum nodes kept warm to meet latency SLOs.
- If demand exceeds reserved baseline we have configurable burst policies:
  * Auto-burst to shared spare capacity (best-effort)
  * Autoscale within reserved pool up to a configured max (if commit allows)
  * Policy-based fallback to a compatible CPU/quantized variant to preserve correctness at degraded throughput

For the POC I recommend the following runbook (attached as poc-runbook.md):
- Day 0: Provision reserved pool (N1 nodes, exact size depends on your QPS targets).
- Day 1: Baseline latency runs at 256/512 tokens, concurrency 1/8/16 — capture P50/P95/P99 and KV cache hit rate.
- Day 2: 24h soak at target sustained QPS, followed by 30m spike test (3x sustained).
- Day 3: Fault injection: kill one node and validate fallback and rebalancing behavior.

Metrics we will capture: P50/P95/P99 latencies, tokens/sec, cost-per-token (incl. reserved amortization), cache-hit ratio, pre-warm time.

I can present the detailed runbook on the kickoff call Wednesday. If you have a preferred model family (we'll mirror your hyperscaler model family where possible) share the model name and quantization preference.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
